question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be two continuous random variables with the following conditional probability density function:

$$
{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{2x+2y}{2y+1}, & \,0<x<1,\,0<y<1 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

Find $P(X<\frac{3}{4}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}).$
question.worked_solution:
Recall that 

$$
P(X\in A\,|\,Y=y)={\int }_{A}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)\,\text{d}x,
$$

where ${f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is the conditional probability density function of $X$ given $Y=y.$ 

In our case, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X<\frac{3}{4}\,|\,Y=\frac{1}{2}) & ={\int }_{0}^{3/4}{f}_{X\,|\,Y}(x\,|\,y=\frac{1}{2})\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{3/4}\frac{(2x+2\cdot \frac{1}{2})}{(2\cdot \frac{1}{2}+1)}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}{\int }_{0}^{3/4}(2x+1)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[{x}^{2}+x]_{0}^{3/4} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({(\frac{3}{4})}^{2}+\frac{3}{4}-0) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(\frac{9}{16}+\frac{3}{4}) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot \frac{21}{16} \\  & =\frac{21}{32}.\end{aligned}
$$
